newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Semis - Bid tone returns on Vic sale.
newsitem.headline: Australian Semis - Bid tone returns on Vic sale.

text.p: *Semis bonds are attracting a bid tone again, led by buying of TCV stock, which is being linked to the sale of the Victorian power generator, Loy Yang A.
Semi-government bonds are attracting a bid tone again, led by buying of Treasury Corp of Victoria (TCV) stock, which some traders are linking to the sale of the Victorian power generator, Loy Yang A.
Previous privatisation sales have resulted in debt reductions for the Victorian state and has been one of the major planks in raising its credit rating profile.
Confirmation that a consortium led by U.S. utilities CMS Energy Corp and NRG Energy Inc have succefully won the A$4.75 billion bid is due to be made later on Tuesday.
"There was been reasonably aggressive buying of semis and TCV has been well bid," said one trader.

This has helped the semis market return to a tightening spread bias against Australian Treasury bonds, having been under some pressure in recent weeks as the impact of a series of favourable comments in March by the major credit agencies began to fade.

Indeed, domestic institutions were seen as sellers last week when Australian Treasury bonds were rallying in anticipation of favourable reports this week on wages and inflation, causing spread differentials to widen.
Another trader, while not disputing the link between the semis buying and the Loy Yang A sale, said the current rally was being made on fairly thin volume.
And "We've known about this sale for sometime, so why it's coming to notice now beats me. But buyers are back, having been offered for the past week and half," he said.

Meanwhile, Australian debt markets are hanging out for the long awaited verdict by the Australian Industrial Relations Commission on the "living wage" claim due at 2.00 p.m. (0400 GMT) on Tuesday and the March quarter CPI on Wednesday.
